I really have a hard time agreeing with Jim on this one. Though the examples of bad games ( Basically no art design what-so-ever) are valid he is missing one point. As the indi scene grows both the number of good and bad games from the indi scene grow with it. The Unity game engine allows indi studios to compete with AAA studios because of how cost effective, easy to use and accessible it is as an engine. That means some awesome games are going to be made on very small budgets and so will some terrible ones.

It's the equivalent of if there was a movie theatre chain that only played college and university student films. Some would be awesome and completely worth the ticket but there is going to be alot of shit simply because of lack of budget, experience and tools that students work with.

In other words it's completely fair to call them out on poor design, bugs and bad art design but its a given not some sort of epidemic.

It is a given that there will be some poor games in the mix, but I think the underlying cause for the increase would be the Steam Green light system. Lazy developers can produce tons of games using basic assets, and the Green light system, as it is now, allows these games to be shotgunned into the market. I agree with you that there will always be bad games and lazy developers, but a lot of these can be prevented by a reworking of the system.
